external_invariants: Model is pretrained microsoft/resnet-18 loaded from the local assets directory (local_files_only, no downloads) with dtype float32, in eval mode, on context['device'].

Numerical policies from common.configure(): torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False, torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest'), torch.manual_seed(20261020), set_num_threads(4).
Input batch is exactly images[torch.arange(32, device=cuda) % 3].contiguous() from pixels.npy; data, batch size 32, layout NCHW 224x224 and float32 dtype are unchanged.
The forward runs under torch.inference_mode() with model.eval(); no dropout, sampling or randomness is involved.
run() executes the complete workload (single forward producing full logits for all 32 images); no work is moved outside the measured boundary and no extra synchronization semantics are altered.
Correctness observation schema is {logits: full (32, num_classes) logits tensor, top1: argmax class indices}; logits must satisfy atol=rtol=1e-4 and top1 must match exactly.
latency_ms is wall time of the full workload with CUDA synchronization at both boundaries, matching the source's measured region.
images_per_second is derived from the unchanged work amount: batch * 1000 / elapsed_ms.

peak_allocated_bytes is torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() with the watermark reset before the timed region, as in the source; the memory goal carries the constraint images_per_second >= 0.95 * baseline ratio.
No accuracy or convergence claim beyond the source's reference-fidelity checks (close_check on logits, exact top1, negative corruption control).

selection.rationale: Current evidence (accepted bundle trial-25dfd4d7ca, clean latency_ms 3.633) makes the GPU the critical path: in observations/current/execution_timeline the 70 kernels span 3500.9 us with 3420.8 us active union and only 80.1 us of gaps, and the host submits everything before a 293 us final cudaDeviceSynchronize drain, so only GPU-kernel-time removal moves latency_ms materially. Convolutions are 2971 us (85%, cudnn heuristic winograd/scudnn, TF32 and benchmark frozen off) and are near the practical fp32 floor; the remaining addressable fat is non-conv kernels plus conv-site tier inconsistencies, all owned by one coherent editable region, the pooler plus the 8 ResNetBasicLayer residual blocks whose children include all conv sites: (1) max_pool_forward_nchw on [32,64,112,224] costs 189.2 us (5.4%) while moving ~180 MB (it writes a 51.4 MB int64 indices tensor the workload never reads) = ~0.95 TB/s effective, versus 4.03 TB/s achieved by the add_ vectorized kernel on a same-size tensor in the same trace - a ~4x bandwidth gap; (2) the 8 residual add_ (77.2 us) + post-residual ReLU (62.4 us) pairs are two full memory passes that one fused add+relu kernel can execute for the add cost alone (~139.6 -> ~80 us); (3) steady-state trace contradicts the previous bundle's per-site calibration on identical shapes: at 64x64x3x3 the fused sites total 229.6/226.4 us while the conv2d+relu_ fallback sites total 238.8/238.1 us (same for 128 and 256 channel shapes), so re-tiering the 8 fallback conv sites (F.conv2d + separate relu_ kernel ~76 us total) to the fused epilogue path saves ~40 us more. Region boundary: MaxPool2d (embedder.pooler), all 4 ResNetBasicLayer groups, and the 5 ResNetConvLayer + 3 ResNetShortCut groups of the accepted bundle, so the earlier whole bundle is explicitly replaced rather than composed around; BasicLayer replacements must still dispatch through layer[0]/layer[1]/shortcut module boundaries so the conv-site replacements actually execute (no graph capture - replay would skip the Python dispatch the coverage counts).
selection.hypothesis: Three exact-numerics edits inside this region remove ~200-235 us of GPU time from the 3484 us kernel path, taking clean latency_ms from ~3.63 to ~3.40-3.43 ms (-5.5 to -6.5%) with paired gains expected to exceed the prior MAD noise bounds (~0.01-0.04 ms): (a) replace MaxPool2d's forward with an index-free fused max-pool kernel (Triton 3.7.1 is in the measured worker env; compile at build/warmup outside timing) computing the same 3x3/s2/p1 NCHW max - max is exact, so logits and top1 are bitwise unchanged and the 51.4 MB indices allocation disappears, lowering peak_allocated_bytes; (b) replace each BasicLayer's aten add_ + nn.ReLU pair with one fused add-then-relu kernel (same op order, bitwise identical), invoked after the inherited conv-site module calls so their dispatch remains observed; (c) re-tier the 8 fallback conv sites to cudnn_convolution_relu where the current steady-state trace shows it faster (64/128/256-channel 3x3 shapes) with guarded fallback, explicitly replacing the earlier whole conv bundle. Unknowns to test on the leased GPU, not assume: actual achievable Triton pooling bandwidth on GPU-4bead555 (only ~4 TB/s elementwise evidence exists, no direct pooling measurement), Triton launch overhead net of the 80 us gap budget, and whether fused epilogue holds its trace-measured advantage when re-calibrated in a fresh worker; if pooling tops out at ~2 TB/s the win shrinks to ~95 us and total gain to ~3.5%, still above noise. Risks bounded by per-site guards falling back to current behavior, worst case equal to the accepted 3.633 ms baseline.

proposal.rationale: Previous feedback (trial-25dfd4d7ca, accepted, clean latency_ms 3.633, quality pass with max_abs_error 9.5e-6) changes this attempt in two ways: (1) it is now the baseline to beat and its 20 conv-site call writes overlap this region, so this proposal explicitly replaces the whole installed bundle trial-25dfd4d7ca-param-82f6ef75 and re-provides the folded-BN conv execution itself rather than composing around it; (2) the steady-state observations/current execution_timeline on that accepted state shows the remaining addressable GPU fat outside the conv kernels: max_pool_forward_nchw on [32,64,112,112] costs 189.2 us while writing a 51.4 MB int64 indices tensor the workload never reads (~0.95 TB/s effective, versus 4.03 TB/s achieved by the vectorized add_ kernel on same-sized traffic in the same trace); the 8 residual aten add_ (77.2 us) plus post-residual ReLU (62.4 us) pairs run as two full memory passes; and each of the 11 no-relu folded conv sites (8 layer.1 ConvLayers + 3 ResNetShortCut) launches a separate bias-apply elementwise kernel after its conv kernel (~85 us total in target-resources launch_configurations). Host dispatch is not the critical path (70 kernels span 3500.9 us with 3420.8 us active union, 80.1 us of gaps, host submits everything before a 293 us final drain), so only GPU-kernel-time removal moves latency_ms. This candidate rebuilds the selected region as one coherent composite: (a) the embedder.pooler MaxPool2d site executes an index-free Triton 3x3/stride-2/pad-1 NCHW max kernel (compiled at installation; max is exact, so values are bitwise identical to F.max_pool2d and the 51.4 MB indices allocation disappears, lowering per-run peak_allocated_bytes); (b) each of the 8 ResNetBasicLayer sites dispatches layer[0], layer[1] and shortcut through their physical module boundaries so the installed conv-site replacements actually execute and are counted (no CUDA-graph capture, which would skip the Python dispatch the coverage counts), then fuses the residual epilogue: the preferred tier routes layer.1 through aten::cudnn_convolution_add_relu so conv+bias+add+relu run in one cudnn epilogue (removing the separate bias kernel, the add_ kernel and the relu kernel on those sites); a per-call verified residual handoff (shape/dtype/device-checked tensor left in a per-block channel plus a fused flag the producer must set) decides whether the fused result may be returned directly - correctness never depends on the handoff: when the flag is absent (wrapper guard fallback, calibration rejection, or any exception) the block computes one Triton add+relu kernel, relu(a+b) in place on the layer.1 output the composite owns, replacing the separate add_ and relu passes; (c) the 20 conv sites keep the accepted bundle's behavior: eval BatchNorm2d folded into the conv weight and a derived bias, tiered per site at installation by calibration (cudnn_convolution_relu for the 9 relu sites when compliant and not slower, F.conv2d on folded tensors otherwise, parent on any failure). Expected effect against the observed trace: pooling 189.2 us -> ~45-70 us (actual achievable Triton pooling bandwidth on GPU-4bead555 is unknown until measured; only ~4 TB/s elementwise evidence exists), residual epilogue 139.6 us add_+relu -> ~80 us as a Triton kernel or ~zero marginal cost when absorbed into the add_relu conv epilogue, layer.1 bias kernels ~67 us -> 0 on fused sites: roughly 190-320 us of the 3484 us kernel path, taking clean latency_ms from ~3.63 toward ~3.31-3.44 ms. Every numerics claim is gated per site at installation (atol=rtol=1e-4 elementwise vs the raw parent on seeded synthetic randn inputs; fixture data never read; global RNG untouched) and end-to-end by the frozen quality check; worst case every guard falls back to parents and behavior equals the previously accepted bundle. Consumers of the eliminated calls remain valid: the pooler output feeds stage 1 unchanged (same values, indices never read); the residual add_/relu/activation boundaries are computed by the fused epilogue or the Triton add+relu kernel inside the block replacement; Sequential/Identity container wrappers are subsumed by the block replacement's direct child dispatch; aten conv children of still-dispatched conv sites may re-materialize as observations of the same op identity under the folded weights while the original parent paths (aten.max_pool2d, aten.add_, aten.relu) no longer execute.

setup_work.description: All setup runs on the leased worker inside build(context), outside the timed boundary: (1) eval-BN folding per conv site into derived contiguous fp32 tensors w' (same shape as conv weight) and b' (out_channels), lazily rechecked via parameter/buffer version counters, retained for the candidate lifetime; source parameters and running stats never mutated. (2) Triton kernels (_maxpool3x3_s2 index-free pooling, _add_relu fused epilogue) compile at their first calibration launch; compiled binaries live in the Triton/driver cache, which torch allocator counters do not measure. (3) Per-site calibration on seeded per-call CPU generators (synthetic randn moved to device; fixture pixels never read; torch.manual_seed policy untouched): one raw parent reference execution, elementwise atol=rtol=1e-4 equivalence gate per tier (pooling additionally gated on torch.equal exactness), CUDA-event timing (3 warmup + 8 iterations) of compliant tiers and of the parent, parent chosen when >10% faster. (4) BasicLayer tiers calibrate the whole composed block (layer[0]/shortcut through their chosen conv tiers, layer.1 fused or plain) against the raw block parent, including the cudnn_convolution_add_relu alpha probe (None, then 1.0).
setup_work.retained_memory: Retained folded weights/biases ~44.7 MB plus ~19 KB across the 20 conv sites (same as the accepted bundle this proposal replaces); no other persistent buffers.
setup_work.transient_memory: Calibration transients peak at roughly 300-700 MB (stem-site dominated: 19.2 MB input with ~103 MB tier outputs; pooler-site 102.8 MB input plus the parent's 51.4 MB indices), freed to the caching allocator before runs; they raise framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes and lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes but not the per-run peak_allocated_bytes counter the adapter resets before timing. At runtime the candidate lowers per-run allocations: the 51.4 MB pooler indices tensor and the separate post-residual relu output (up to 25.7 MB per block) are no longer allocated, so per-run peak_allocated_bytes should fall; this is a counter decrease on the declared metric, not a general physical-memory saving.
setup_work.state_and_sync: Warm-model inference lifecycle only: no training, no parameter mutation, no added streams/events, no CUDA graphs, no cudnn/TF32 policy changes; the workload executes on current inputs on every invocation with the source's synchronization boundaries unchanged.

quality_risks: BN folding reassociates fp32 arithmetic (the prior accepted bundle measured 9.5e-6 max end-to-end logits error); the fused add_relu epilogue reassociates conv+bias+add slightly differently than (conv+bias) then +residual; both are bounded per site by the installation 1e-4 elementwise gate against the raw parent and end-to-end by the frozen logits atol=rtol=1e-4 check.

aten::cudnn_convolution_add_relu semantics (alpha, bias application, relu placement) are not assumed: calibration probes alpha in (None, 1.0) and rejects the tier unless relu(conv+bias+residual) matches the raw parent within 1e-4; rejected blocks keep the F.conv2d tier plus the Triton add+relu kernel, still numerically correct.

aten::cudnn_convolution_relu and cudnn_convolution_add_relu expose no allow_tf32 argument; if their epilogue used TF32 the per-site calibration gate would detect the mismatch and route the site to F.conv2d, which carries the global allow_tf32=False policy; the accepted prior bundle already ran 9 sites on cudnn_convolution_relu with 9.5e-6 end-to-end error, evidencing the fp32 path.

Triton pooling is exact max (installation gate torch.equal against F.max_pool2d on synthetic input including border windows; NaN-propagating maximum and relu-keeps-NaN replicated in-kernel), so pooler values are bitwise unchanged; any mismatch routes the site to the parent. relu outputs of -0.0 vs +0.0 can differ only bitwise (absolute difference 0), inside tolerance.
exact_top1 could flip only if accumulated error crossed the top-two logit gap; real-image margins and the 9.5e-6 scale of prior measured error make this unlikely but it is not proven.

The residual handoff is never trusted blindly: the layer.1 replacement consumes the channel only when shape/dtype/device match and sets the fused flag only after the op returns; the block replacement re-checks the flag per call and otherwise computes the Triton add+relu itself, so wrapper guard fallbacks, calibration rejections and exceptions degrade to correct separate kernels rather than wrong values; isolated invocations of the layer.1 site never see the channel and return the plain folded conv.
Per-site timing calibration could mis-rank tiers on a noisy worker; the consequence is only performance (a slower compliant tier or the parent), never correctness.

The cudnn heuristic may pick a slower algorithm for the add_relu epilogue shape; the calibration timing gate then routes that block to the Triton add+relu tier or the parent, bounding the loss to previously accepted behavior.

Guards route to parents on train mode, grad-enabled callers, non-fp32/non-CUDA/mismatched-channel inputs, non-contiguous pooler inputs, unfoldable statistics and any runtime exception (labels: setup_route_parent, setup_unsupported_module, setup_unsupported_normalization, setup_unsupported_activation, setup_fold_unavailable, setup_calibration_failed, setup_parent_fastest, setup_triton_unavailable, setup_exception_parent, guard_unsupported_signature_parent, guard_fold_unavailable_parent, runtime_failure_parent).
